default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-438.title: Low-kurtosis tape micro-break fade
E-438.hypothesis: When the recent 1-bar price changes are thin-tailed compared with the previous sessions (low excess kurtosis), the tape is made of small two-way trades with no jumps from informed size; a 15-minute box break in that tape is a drift of liquidity providers' quotes rather than news, and they lean it back, so fade it.

E-439.title: Outsized break-bar fade
E-439.hypothesis: A break of the short box made by a single bar whose own range is a large share of (or bigger than) the whole box spends the move in one burst of market orders that runs the stops behind the edge; once those stops are filled no initiator is left and the stop-run sellers (buyers) are the other side, so fade the break bar.

E-440.title: Unclustered-volatility micro-break fade
E-440.hypothesis: Volatility normally clusters: a wide bar is followed by another when information arrives. When the lag-1 correlation of bar ranges in the recent window is low, ranges are random noise rather than an information flow, so a 15-minute box break carries no news and the passive side takes it back; fade it.

E-441.title: Close-box break inside the wick box fade
E-441.hypothesis: A close beyond the highest (lowest) close of the window that is still inside the window's wick high (low) only reaches prices that were already offered and rejected intrabar; the sellers who printed the wick are still there and chart traders who buy the closing break are the liquidity, so fade it.

E-442.title: Even-range tape micro-break fade
E-442.hypothesis: When bar ranges over the window are much more uniform than usual (low coefficient of variation versus the previous sessions), price is being walked by steady quoting with no bursts; a 15-minute box break in that tape is the regular oscillation reaching an edge, not an expansion, so fade it.

E-443.title: Fast-reverting deviation micro-break fade
E-443.hypothesis: Fit the AR(1) coefficient of the price's deviation from its rolling mean: when it is below its usual level, deviations die out faster than normal, i.e. inventory-holding market makers are actively pulling price back to the mean; a 15-minute box break in that state is a deviation they will absorb, so fade it.

E-444.title: Balance-of-power exhaustion turn fade
E-444.hypothesis: The rolling mean of (close-open)/(high-low) measures how consistently bars close in the buyers' (sellers') favour; when a stretch of one-sided bar pressure ends (the mean falls back through its threshold), the aggressive side has finished and the late chasers are offside, so trade against the stretch on the turn.

E-445.title: Cash-open price cross fade
E-445.hypothesis: WIN trades from 09:00 but the cash equities open at 10:00, and the price at that moment is where index arbitrage and fund rebalancing set their reference; when price returns from well away and closes through that level, the arbitrage desks defend it as a pivot, so the cross fails more often than not: fade it.

E-446.title: High ordinal-entropy tape micro-break fade
E-446.hypothesis: Permutation entropy of the order of three consecutive closes measures how random the tape is; when it is above its usual level, no ordinal pattern (trend runs) dominates, so nobody is working a directional order and a 15-minute box break is noise that the two-sided book absorbs: fade it.

E-447.title: Rising-floor box break follow
E-447.hypothesis: A box whose lows rose markedly in its second half while the top held (ascending-triangle shape) shows buyers lifting their bids under a fixed seller; when the close breaks the top the seller is exhausted and the stops of shorts who sold the flat top are bought, so follow the break (mirror for a falling ceiling).
